blocks.title: Molar heat of fusion
blocks.text: The amount of heat absorbed by one mole of a solid to melt it into the liquid at its melting point at 1 atmospheric pressure is called molar heat of fusion.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book gives the molar heat of fusion of ice as 4.6 kJ mol⁻¹. The accepted value is 6.01 kJ mol⁻¹ at 0 °C: H₂O(s) → H₂O(l), ΔHf = 6.01 kJ mol⁻¹.
